method: Great-circle station-to-station distances using NOAA public inventory coordinates (mean Earth radius 6371.0088 km). This is a bounded first rollout, not a coast-wide equivalence claim.

choices.exposure: Offshore Santa Barbara Channel reference to offshore Santa Barbara Channel reference. Existing logical nearshore roles also use offshore channel references.
choices.reason: Both stations measure open channel wind and waves south of the mainland and north of the Channel Islands. Backup is a western-channel regional reference, not an estimate at the eastern station or Ventura shore. Local shelter and gradients remain different. No offshore-to-beach substitution.

rejected.46011: Santa Maria is on the exposed coast northwest of Point Conception, outside the sheltered channel; proximity alone does not qualify it.

choices.exposure: Los Angeles outer harbor and Long Beach Terminal Island: adjacent ports in the San Pedro Bay harbor complex.
choices.reason: Both NOAA reference prediction stations provide MLLW high/low water levels in the same harbor complex. Heights and times remain station-specific. Neither predicts entrance current or slack water.

choices.exposure: San Diego Bay harbor reference to another station inside the same bay.
choices.reason: Quarantine Station lies 5.63 km west of Broadway inside San Diego Bay. It is a NOAA subordinate high/low prediction station using Broadway offsets, not an independent observing system. Serves station-specific reference MLLW predictions only; no local current or slack-water claim. A provider-wide outage can affect both.

choices.exposure: Open-ocean NDBC weather buoys on the exposed central coast north of Point Conception: Cape San Martin, 55 NM west-northwest of Morro Bay, and Santa Maria, 21 NM northwest of Point Arguello. Both face the prevailing northwest wind and swell.
choices.reason: Morro Bay's offshore role is a regional open-water wind and wave reference, not a reading at the harbor or the fishing grounds. Santa Maria sits on the same exposed coast and is closer to Estero Bay and Point Buchon than Cape San Martin is. It is a different place: northwest wind usually builds toward Point Arguello, so the backup can read stronger wind than the primary would. The label names 46011 whenever it serves. Same-hour sample 2026-10-12 12:20Z: 46028 3.5 m at 11 s from 324 deg, wind 270 deg 2 m/s; 46011 2.9 m at 11 s from 310 deg, wind 260 deg 3 m/s.

rejected.46259: Santa Lucia Escarpment (CDIP 222) is a wave-only deep-water buoy 117 km from 46028; it reports no wind, so it cannot stand in for the role's wind reading.

unconfigured_policy: Keep all other roles single-station in this bounded rollout: an adjacent station is not evidence of comparable exposure, and offshore wind buoys are not substitutes for CDIP nearshore wave sensors. Never substitute tide heights across a headland, harbor or island without a separate review.
